articles.author: ohmygod
articles.description:
Your Anchor program has 100% branch coverage. Every instruction handler has a matching unit test. Clippy is clean. anchor test passes.
Then someone calls withdraw() after deposit() after update_oracle() in the same transaction, and 40,000 SOL vanishes into an attacker's wallet.
Unit tests verify the paths you imagined. Fuzzers find the paths you didn't.
This guide walks through Trident — Ackee Blockchain Security's open-source Rust fuzzer for Solana Anchor programs — and shows you how to catch real vulnerability classes before auditors (or attackers) do.
Solana programs are stateful, multi-account, and composable. A single instruction can read from 8+ accounts, each with their own owner, data layout, and lifecycle. The attack surface isn't just "bad input" — it's bad sequences of valid inp…
articles.title: Fuzzing Solana Programs with Trident: How Ackee's Open-Source Fuzzer Catches Bugs That Unit Tests Miss

articles.description:
Every January, millions of workers stare at their PTO balance and think: "That's not enough." They're wrong. They have plenty. They're just spending it wrong.
Five vacation days, placed strategically around holidays you already get for free, can buy you 18 consecutive days off in 2026. No negotiation with your manager. No unpaid leave. No tricks.
I call it the 5:18 Formula, and it works because most people don't realize that where you spend your PTO matters more than how much you have.
In France, this concept has a name: faire le pont — "making the bridge." A Thursday holiday? Everyone takes Friday off. Tuesday holiday? Take Monday. The entire country has been coordinating around this for over a century.
The math is simple: a random Tuesday off gives you one day of rest. That same Tuesday …
articles.title: "The 5:18 Formula: How 5 PTO Days Become 18 Consecutive Days Off in 2026"
